label: Gresset 2002
setting: community-residing elderly; home interview and home visual examination
recruitment: Stage 1: random sample of community residents aged 65+ in Quebec (CSHA 1991-1992; 1777 completed, 98.7%; ages 75+ oversampled). Stage 2 (validation): Montreal-area subjects not eligible for other CSHA components; all positives plus a random sample of negatives; 144 eligible, 31 lost, 42 refused, 6 unscheduled, 65 examined (45.1%); work-up (verification) bias acknowledged
cohort: Canadian Study of Health and Aging, Quebec community sample (stage 2 is a subsample of Montreal-area participants)
notes: Stage 1 sex: 1106 women and 671 men of 1777 (p3). Stage 2 age/sex of the 65 examined NR. VA ETDRS charts at 4 m (distance) and modified near ETDRS chart at 0.4 m; VA measured presenting and best-corrected; classified by best eye (p2). Examiner (first author) blind to questionnaire answers. Crude sens/spec cannot be applied to an unselected population because sampling fractions differed by test result (p2). Only functional (presenting VA) impairment tabulated, because after refraction only 2 subjects changed from mild impairment to none (p3). Paper title/abstract frames the study as prevalence and rehabilitation-service utilization; abstract PPV 21% and NPV 100% refer to moderate or worse
